metaTitle: Focus Session: How Long It Should Be and What to Work On
metaDescription: A focus session is protected time for one demanding task. Compare 25-minute and 90-minute sessions, choose the right work for them, and let GAIA schedule them.
definition: A focus session is a dedicated, scheduled period of uninterrupted time committed to a single task or project, protected from notifications, meetings, and other interruptions to enable sustained deep work.
extendedDescription: A focus session operationalizes the deep work concept into a concrete, schedulable unit. Typically 60 to 180 minutes long, focus sessions create the conditions for high-quality output by removing the context-switching that degrades complex cognitive work. The session has a clear start time, defined task, and protected boundaries. Notifications are silenced, meetings are blocked, and the single task receives full attention. Focus sessions work best when scheduled in advance on the calendar rather than pursued opportunistically in the gaps between other commitments.
howGaiaUsesIt: GAIA schedules focus sessions on your calendar based on task priorities and your energy patterns. During a focus session, GAIA holds non-urgent notifications, declines meeting requests, and only interrupts for genuinely urgent items.

faqs.question: How long should a focus session be?
faqs.answer: Research on sustained attention suggests 90-minute sessions align with natural ultradian rhythm cycles. The Pomodoro Technique uses 25-minute blocks. GAIA can schedule focus sessions of your preferred length based on task type and your calendar availability.

faqs.question: What should I work on during a focus session?
faqs.answer: Focus sessions are best reserved for cognitively demanding work that benefits from uninterrupted attention: writing, coding, strategic planning, complex analysis. GAIA helps identify which tasks on your list warrant focus session treatment based on deadline and complexity.
